resources.string: Measure your pupillary distance (PD) with the front camera.
No objects needed. Uses the average iris diameter (or your value calibrated with a card) as reference.
Hold a standard-size card (credit card, bank or loyalty card) on your forehead. More accurate, and it can calibrate the iris method.
Iris reference: average value %1$s mm (not calibrated)
Iris reference: %1$s mm (calibrated with a card)
PD Measure uses the front camera to locate your eyes. Images are processed only on this device and are never saved or sent.
Face not detected: look at the screen in good light
Keep your head straight and look into the camera
Move back a little (≈ %1$s cm, best 30–50 cm)
Remove your glasses, hold the phone at eye level 30–50 cm away and look straight into the front camera, not at the screen.
Remove your glasses. Press a standard card flat and horizontal on your forehead, just above the eyebrows, look into the camera and take the photo.
Drag the two lines onto the left and right edges of the card. Tap near a line to select it and use the arrows for fine adjustment.
Also calibrate the iris method (measured iris: %1$s mm)
Measured iris %1$s mm is outside the plausible range: check the lines. Calibration not available.
Mono PD: right %1$s mm · left %2$s mm
Indicative measurement, not a medical device. For prescription lenses rely on the measurement taken by your optician.

The app finds pupils and irises with an on-device face landmark model. The distance between the pupils in pixels is converted to millimetres using a reference of known size: the iris diameter (11.7 mm on average, or your calibrated value) or the width of a standard card (85.60 mm). Since your eyes converge on the camera, the near PD is converted to distance PD using the estimated camera distance.
The app has no internet permission. Camera frames are analysed in memory and never saved or sent anywhere.
Each attempt is the median of 45 frames. Attempts are averaged; with 5 attempts the highest and lowest are discarded.
Look away, reposition the phone and press Continue for attempt %1$d of %2$d.
Camera distance not available: values are not corrected for convergence (distance PD is usually 2–3 mm larger).
Spread %1$s mm: inconsistent, repeat in better light or calibrate with the card
Highest and lowest attempts excluded from the average.
Intermediate and reading values refer to the lens plane (12 mm vertex distance). The measured row is the raw value with the eyes converging on the camera. OD = right eye, OS = left eye.
What to enter in an online order form
Progressive or multifocal lenses: enter the two monocular numbers if the form allows it. Always use distance values: the lab calculates the near zone from the addition (ADD).
Reading-only glasses: only if the form explicitly asks for the near PD, enter %1$s (OD %2$s · OS %3$s). Otherwise enter the distance PD and select reading use.
Values rounded to 0.5 mm; OD + OS equals the binocular PD.
